​1. Platform Overview​
​Plexo Sales Rep Portal (“Plexo”) is a two-portal web application built to run an independent​
​sales representative network. It gives sales representatives a self-service portal to manage their​
​own profile, agreements, and training/marketing resources, and gives internal administrators a​
​management console to onboard representatives, curate shared content, and keep track of​
​compliance documentation and payout details across the network.​
​The application is delivered as a single-page web application with two independently gated​
​sections — a Rep Portal and an Admin Portal — served from one shell application and backed​
​by a dedicated REST API and a SQL Server database. A personalized “portal link” lets an​
​individual representative sign in directly without filling in a login form, which is intended to make​
​the link easy to share as part of onboarding or marketing outreach.​
​2. Architecture Overview​
​The application follows a conventional three-tier architecture: a browser-based single-page​
​application, a REST API, and a relational database, with outbound email handled as a​
​supporting service.​

​●​
​Client:​​An Angular single-page application renders​​both the Rep Portal and the Admin​
​Portal from one shell, and communicates with the backend exclusively over HTTP.​

​●​
​API:​​A REST API exposes the application's business​​domains (representatives,​
​documents, bank details, training/marketing content, notes, email settings, and support​
​requests) as a set of resource-oriented endpoints.​

​●​
​Database:​​A relational database persists representative​​records and everything​
​associated with them (documents, bank details, notes) along with shared content​
​(training/marketing library, links, and the welcome-email template).​

​●​
​Email:​​Transactional email (the new-representative​​welcome email) and internal​
​notification email (the three “contact the admin team” flows) are sent through a shared​
​HTML templating layer and an SMTP relay.​
​On the client, state that needs to be shared across screens (the representative directory, the​
​signed-in session, document and content libraries) is held in a small number of dedicated “store”​
​services built on Angular's reactive signals, with each store composing the API calls needed to​
​keep its data current. This keeps every screen that depends on the same data — for example a​
​representative's own profile page and the admin's detail view of that same representative —​
​automatically in sync without a manual refresh.​
​Both portals sit behind their own client-side sign-in guard, so a representative session does not​
​grant access to the Admin Portal and vice versa. Section 3.3 describes the sign-in flow itself,​
​and Section 7 (Sourcing Notes) records the current limits of this access-control model.​
​3. Workflow​
​At a high level, a representative signs in to manage their own profile and resources, while an​
​administrator signs in to manage the full roster of representatives and the shared content both​
​portals draw on. The two workflows below describe what each audience can do; Section 3.3​
​covers how sign-in works, and Section 3.4 summarizes the journey end to end.​
​3.1 Rep Portal​
​The Rep Portal is where a signed-in representative manages their own information and​
​resources. Key functionalities include:​

​●​
​Overview:​​A personal dashboard showing an onboarding​​checklist and progress bar​
​(contact info, sales-lead link, agreement, tax form, certification, consultant fee, business​
​card, and portal-credential milestones), plus a one-click way to copy the representative's​
​personal portal link.​

​●​
​Profile:​​A view of the representative's contact​​information, address, certification and​
​consultant-fee status, and their assigned relationships (who referred them, and which​
​senior consultant they are assigned to). Includes a self-service business-card approval​
​workflow — a representative can approve an admin-submitted business-card proof or​
​request changes.​

​●​
​Sales Leads:​​A single page presenting the representative's​​personal sales-lead link for​
​sharing with prospects.​

​●​
​Agreements & Forms:​​The representative's own​​agreement, pricing sheet, and​
​presentation materials (view/download, managed by the admin team) alongside a​
​self-service upload for their W-9 tax form.​

​●​
​Training Hub:​​Admin-curated training material and FAQs, a knowledge-base link, and​
​a library the representative can browse, filter by language, and contribute their own​
​training resources to.​

​●​
​Marketing Hub:​​Product and dashboard walkthrough​​videos, shared pricing materials,​
​and a filterable library of marketing assets (images, PDFs, documents, and videos)​
​available to view or download.​

​●​
​Documents & Instructions:​​A read-only library​​of shared setup instructions (email​
​setup, contract-wizard instructions, W-9 template).​

​●​
​Contact Us:​​A support form for messaging the admin​​team directly from within the​
​portal.​
​3.2 Admin Portal​
​The Admin Portal is where internal staff manage the representative roster and the content both​
​portals rely on. Key functionalities include:​

​●​
​Reps Directory:​​A searchable, filterable roster​​of every representative with status and​
​document-completeness indicators, summary statistics, and a guided multi-step wizard​
​for onboarding a new representative.​

​●​
​Rep Detail Console:​​The most detailed screen​​in the application — a single​
​representative's full record, covering contact and address information, referral​
​relationships, resource links, certification and consultant-fee status, bank details, admin​
​and shared notes, portal credentials, document management (upload/replace/delete for​
​every document type), and account status, plus the ability to resend the welcome email​
​or remove the representative.​

​●​
​Training Hub Admin:​​Manages the fixed Training​​Hub materials (training PDF, FAQ),​
​the knowledge-base link, and provides an oversight table of every document every​
​representative has uploaded, system-wide.​

​●​
​Marketing Hub Admin:​​Full management of the​​marketing resource library, the four​
​product/dashboard video links, and the shared marketing pricing documents.​

​●​
​Email Settings:​​An editor for the new-representative​​welcome-email subject and​
​body, with insertable merge tokens and a live preview.​

​●​
​Documents & Instructions:​​Manages the shared​​instruction documents that​
​representatives see in a read-only capacity.​
​3.3 Authentication & Access​
​Representatives sign in with their email address and their numeric Representative ID;​
​administrators sign in with an email address and password on a separate tab of the same​
​screen. A successful sign-in is kept in the browser for the duration of the session so the portal​
​remains open across page reloads.​
​Visiting a representative's personal portal link (for example, as shared from the Overview​
​screen) resolves the representative automatically and signs them in without displaying the login​
​form, falling back to the manual form if the link cannot be resolved.​
​The Rep Portal and Admin Portal are gated independently, so being signed in to one does not​
​grant access to the other. The current scope and limitations of this model — including that it​
​governs navigation within the application rather than the API itself — are recorded candidly in​
​Section 7 (Sourcing Notes).​
​3.4 Overall User Workflow​
​The primary journey, for either audience, follows the same shape:​
​Sign In → Land on Dashboard → Browse / Manage Records → Upload or Update​
​Information → Get Support or Sign Out​
​The interface is web-based and responsive, collapsing the side navigation into an overlay​
​drawer on narrower screens so the same portal is usable on desktop or mobile without a​
​separate build.​

​5.1 Data Model Overview​

​●​
​Representative:​​The core entity — identity, profile​​and address, resource links,​
​certification/status/business-card flags, referral relationships, and encrypted portal​
​credentials.​

​●​
​Documents:​​Per-representative uploaded file metadata​​(kind, file name, storage path,​
​upload timestamp).​

​●​
​Training Hub Content & Links:​​Uploaded asset metadata​​for the training/marketing​
​library, and the single shared record of static links.​

​●​
​Bank Details:​​Encrypted payout bank information,​​one record per representative.​

​●​
​Notes:​​Free-text notes keyed by representative and​​note kind (admin-only or shared).​

​●​
​Welcome Email Settings:​​The single editable email​​template record, including merge​
​tokens.​

​●​
​Support Requests:​​Transient payloads for the three​​contact flows — emailed directly​
​rather than stored.​
​5.2 Supporting Services​

​●​
​Encryption Service:​​Provides AES-256 encryption​​and decryption for sensitive fields​
​at rest — bank details and portal credential fields.​

​●​
​Email Service:​​Sends transactional and notification​​email over SMTP, rendering​
​shared HTML templates provided by PlexoCommon.​

​6. Sourcing Notes​
​This overview was compiled by reviewing the application's underlying source code — its routing,​
​screens, controllers, and services — rather than from a separate written specification. It reflects​
​how the application currently behaves as of this review, and is intended as a functional​
​reference rather than a design document.​
​A few points are worth keeping in mind when relying on this profile:​

​●​
​Authentication scope:​​Sign-in on both portals​​validates credentials, but the resulting​
​session is not carried forward as a token that the API itself checks on each request. In its​
​current state, the API does not independently authenticate or authorize requests — this​
​is worth addressing before the application is reachable outside a trusted network.​

​●​
​Admin credentials:​​The admin sign-in path currently​​checks a single configured​
​credential pair rather than a managed set of admin accounts. A proper admin identity​
​and role model is recommended before wider rollout.​

​●​
​Configuration & secrets:​​Database, encryption,​​and email-sending credentials are​
​currently stored directly in the API's configuration file rather than a secrets manager.​
​These should be rotated and externalized as part of hardening the application for​
​production use.​

​●​
​Cross-origin policy:​​The API currently accepts​​requests from any origin. This should​
​be scoped to the application's known front-end origins before public release.​

​●​
​API documentation exposure:​​The interactive​​API documentation​
​(Swagger/OpenAPI) is available without an environment check; consider restricting it to​
​non-production environments.​

​●​
​File storage:​​Uploaded documents and training/marketing​​assets are currently stored​
​on the API server's local disk at a fixed path rather than a managed storage service —​
​worth revisiting for scaling or multi-instance deployment.​

​●​
​Commission tracking:​​The Commission screen exists in the Rep Portal but is not​
​currently linked from the visible navigation, and shows placeholder ($0) data — the​
​backend does not yet model actual commission transactions.​

​●​
​Legacy route:​​An older “Documents” screen, superseded​​by “Agreements & Forms,”​
​remains reachable by direct URL though it is no longer linked from navigation.​

​●​
​Saved templates:​​The two blank document templates​​(Agreement, W-4) shown to​
​representatives are currently held in the browser session rather than served from the​
​backend, and reset on refresh.​

​●​
​Scaffolding:​​A default sample endpoint from the​​API project template remains in the​
​codebase and is not part of the business functionality.​

​●​
​Environment configuration:​​The front end's default​​(non-production) configuration​
​points at a local development instance of the API rather than a distinct staging​
​environment.​
